# Evidrift

> Evidrift is a local-first CLI that turns failing JSON requests into replay-verified reductions and revalidates explicit TypeScript or OpenAPI assumptions when contracts drift.

## Try it

- ReproMin demo: `npx --yes evidrift@latest repro-demo`
- Contract-drift demo: `npx --yes evidrift@latest demo`
- Initialize a repository: `npx --yes evidrift@latest init`
- Real CLI demo animation: https://bm1016bm-svg.github.io/evidrift/assets/evidrift-demo.gif
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/evidrift
- Source: https://github.com/bm1016bm-svg/evidrift

## Deterministic evidence

- `minimize`: replays JSON candidates against a literal loopback target and accepts a reduction only when HTTP status plus explicit error identity still match.
- Reproduction artifacts: content-address the minimized request and predicate, preserve bounded probe evidence, and can be verified once with `evidrift reproduce`.
- `typescript.symbol`: records the installed package version, resolved declaration path, selected overload or parameter, normalized call signature, and signature hash.
- `json.pointer`: records a canonical value from a repository-local OpenAPI JSON or JSON Schema file through RFC 6901 JSON Pointer.
- Receipt integrity: canonical serialization plus content-addressed SHA-256 identifiers; saved status fields are never trusted by `evidrift check`.

## Agent integrations

- Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor use the same local STDIO MCP server.
- Agents request Receipt creation through MCP; they do not write trusted verification results directly.
- MCP setup: https://github.com/bm1016bm-svg/evidrift/blob/main/docs/mcp.md

## Deliberate limits

Evidrift does not prove code correct, identify root cause, claim a global minimum, fetch arbitrary URLs, resolve remote OpenAPI references, execute dependency code, or use an LLM judge in CI. ReproMin is CLI-only and limited to explicit loopback replay; contract checks and MCP remain network-free.
